summary: L7 proxy GOAWAY injection causes intermittent gRPC stream truncation for large-model streaming on Private deploy (us-east)
description: Issue summary: Customers on a Private deployment (SigmaDocs) reported intermittent truncation of gRPC streaming responses when requesting long-form outputs (models: gpt-xl-32k, opt-30b-stream). Partial transcripts are returned and the client receives gRPC UNAVAILABLE or INTERNAL after a partial stream. Impact: Production traffic experienced degraded UX for users performing document synthesis; approx 7% of streaming requests fail for large responses during peak windows. Environment: Private deployment in us-east (VPCE + corporate L7 inspection proxy in front of VPCE egress). Steps to reproduce: 1) POST /v1/streams generation request for a prompt that induces >30k tokens of output using model gpt-xl-32k behind customer's L7 proxy. 2) Observe partial streaming followed by a final gRPC error (UNAVAILABLE/14) or HTTP/2 GOAWAY in proxy logs. Observed logs/metrics: - Serving node logs show stream closed with transport error after ~30s of streaming. - Customer's proxy (Bluecoat) logs show GOAWAY frames emitted with last_stream_id set; reason field empty/NO_ERROR. - TCP captures show no TLS alerts and connection remains open for a short time after GOAWAY. - Client shows okhttp errors indicating stream ID exhaustion or stream reuse attempts. Temporary workaround used by customer: 1) Route streaming traffic through a proxy bypass (direct VPCE egress) eliminated the failure. 2) Lowered chunked token window on client to force more frequent flushes (reduced failure rate but not fully mitigated). Investigation summary: Hypothesis: Customer L7 proxy is configured to aggressively insert GOAWAY frames when concurrent HTTP/2 stream count or stream lifetime thresholds are hit. For long-lived, high-throughput streaming (large models) proxy sends GOAWAY which causes an in-flight stream to be terminated mid-response; some client stacks mis-handle the transition leading to partial transcripts instead of a clean retry. Evidence: - Proxy logs correlate GOAWAY timestamps with truncated streams. - Increasing "max_concurrent_streams" on a test proxy reduced occurrences. - Bypassing the proxy eliminated failures. Root cause: Proxy-level HTTP/2 lifecycle management (GOAWAY injection / stream limit enforcement) combined with client library behavior leads to non-idempotent partial results when long-lived streaming responses are terminated without graceful handoff. Next steps and remediation: 1) Customer to update L7 proxy config to: a) disable GOAWAY injection for VPCE-to-Redwood control plane/streaming endpoints or b) increase max_concurrent_streams and stream lifetime limits. 2) Redwood to add a server-side guard: detect GOAWAY mid-stream and emit a clear final trailer indicating retryability where possible, plus guidance in our private-deploy runbook. 3) Recommend customers configure ALPN passthrough / avoid HTTP/2 rewriting for streaming routes. Resolution: Customer updated proxy to allow HTTP/2 pass-through for /v1/streams and increased max_concurrent_streams; the error rate dropped to <0.1% during the monitoring window. Follow-up: Engineering PR created to add clearer final trailer when terminating streams (see related PR).

investigation_notes: Test harness: replayed large-model streaming workload against customer-like proxy (Bluecoat) with configurable concurrent-stream limits. Observed direct correlation between GOAWAY emission and truncated streams. Confirmed bypass and config change mitigations. Proposed fix for runtime: emit explicit 'retryable: true' trailer when we detect forced mid-stream termination to help client-side retry policies.
resolution: Customer reconfigured corporate L7 proxy to pass HTTP/2 streams for /v1/streams and increased max_concurrent_streams; Redwood delivered a runtime change to add a clear trailer on forced stream termination. Monitoring shows issue resolved (failure rate <0.1%).
